messages:
alex: quick flag — noticed a ~4.6% delta between invoice-preview and final ledger for a subset of customers using the proxy-shim routing policy this week. looks correlated with retries and route attr strip in the sidecar.

maria: ugh. which attribute is being stripped?

alex: route_tag header. when the proxy-shim retries it emits a new event that loses route_tag on a small percent of messages (seen on canary env). sample count low but affects high-volume tenants so preview is off.

jamal: can you paste a sample event or query?

alex: pasted a quick kafka tail —

```
kafka-console-consumer --topic metering-events --offset latest-100 --max-messages 50 | jq '. | {tenant,op,tags}'
# result: {tenant: "t-123", op: "token_account", tags: {}}  <-- route_tag missing
```

sasha: is this only the shim or also the legacy router?

alex: shim only so far. legacy router retains header. likely regression from the retry wrapper we shipped last month.

kyle: what are options? hotfix the shim to preserve headers, or add a defensive enrich step in the ingest pipeline to reconstruct route_tag from request_fingerprint?

maria: reconstructing is messy and may misattribute. prefer keeping original header. hotfix + small canary sounds right.

jamal: we should also show a clear signal in console so customers see preview vs ledger divergence for routes. right now ops just see totals.

sasha: agree. a remediation UX could be: console -> Billing -> Invoice preview -> a per-route "missing-tags" heatmap and an example event. toggle to show raw event.

maria: +1. we can wire an alert when preview delta > 1% for any top-10 tenants. ops page can link to trace.

alex: for immediate triage I pushed a debug roll to the shim canary (deploy-bot: deploy canary shim v1.12.3-canary). will monitor.

billing-bot: snapshot: invoice_preview.delta_summary {window: "1h", pct_delta: 4.62, affected_tenants: 3, rule: "proxy-shim"}

kyle: if canary fix passes, we need a backfill plan for lost route_tag events. backfill needs to be idempotent and stamped with original request_ts. otherwise invoices doublecount.

jamal: backfill approach idea: reprocess raw rdlogs, join by request_id, only emit missing-tag events if ledger has no prior event for that request_id. that reduces doublecount risk. but compute cost might be high for multi-day windows.

maria: do we have telemetry to estimate reprocess cost? console should show estimated compute/time for a backfill run. ops will want an ETA.

alex: rough numbers: reprocessing 24h of raw logs for affected partitions ~ 12h on current cluster; could parallelize to 3h with autoscale (ballpark).

sasha: smaller ask — can we add a soft-warning in invoice preview UI when a route attr appears in <= 97% of events? like "route attr coverage: 92% — invoice preview may be incomplete". low effort and lowers support tickets.

maria: good UX. also expose a link "show samples" which pulls 10 raw events and a suggested query to run locally.

alex: plan from here: 1) hotfix shim -> promote canary to 50% if passes 1h, 2) add console soft-warning and per-route coverage metric (small frontend + new metric pipeline), 3) schedule backfill window if customers request credits (ops/sales will decide), 4) postmortem and add unit test for header preservation in retry wrapper.

jamal: timeline estimation?

alex: hotfix canary -> 1h monitor -> 50% -> 6h monitor -> full. console metric — 2 dev days (backend + frontend). backfill scoping — 1 day to produce cost estimate.

kyle: watch out for billing implications. finance needs a clear delta report before issuing credits. make an exact list of affected invoices (ids) and deltas.

maria: will coordinate with finance and support to assemble affected-invoices.csv once we have backfill estimates.

deploy-bot: canary deployment started for shim-service version v1.12.3-canary at 2025-05-04T16:05:12Z

sasha: thanks all. if anyone sees more tenants affected or different route patterns, drop here. i'll file a small RFC for the console coverage metric so design/pm can review. :thumbsup:

alex: updating dashboard alerting now — will post metrics in ~15m.

maria: thanks team.
